meta.title: Illustrative material impact factors
meta.status: ILLUSTRATIVE — prototype screening values, not certified LCA data
meta.boundary: Cradle-to-gate production of 1 kg of material (extraction to finished raw material).
meta.note: Values are rounded, order-of-magnitude figures chosen to sit inside ranges commonly reported in public literature (e.g. ICE Database, Plastics Europe eco-profiles, World Steel, International Aluminium Institute, Textile Exchange). They vary strongly by region, supplier and production route. Replace this file with a licensed LCA database for real decisions.

materials.name: Virgin plastic (PET)
materials.basis: Illustrative; within the range commonly reported for fossil-based PET/PP resin production.
materials.notes: Fossil feedstock. Lightweight and durable, but persistent if littered.

alternatives.cost: Recycled resin is often priced at a small premium (or discount) to virgin depending on the market; food-grade recycled PET usually carries a premium.
alternatives.feasibility_note: Drop-in replacement on most existing moulding equipment; supply of food-grade grades can be limited.
trade_offs: Colour and clarity can be less consistent than virgin resin.
Food-contact applications need certified recycled grades.
Assumes a 1:1 mass substitution; some designs need slightly more material.

materials.name: Recycled plastic (rPET)
materials.basis: Illustrative; mechanical recycling with the cut-off approach (no burden from the first life).
materials.notes: Benefit depends on collection, sorting and reprocessing energy.

materials.name: Aluminium (primary)
materials.basis: Illustrative; primary aluminium ranges widely (roughly 4–20 kg CO2e/kg) depending on smelter electricity.
materials.notes: Very energy-intensive to smelt; highly recyclable with little quality loss.

alternatives.cost: Secondary aluminium is typically cost-competitive with primary; alloy availability can affect price.
alternatives.feasibility_note: Widely available for cast and many wrought alloys.
trade_offs: Some high-purity or aerospace alloys limit recycled content.
Scrap supply is finite — high recycled content in one product can displace it elsewhere.

materials.name: Recycled aluminium
materials.basis: Illustrative; remelting scrap with the cut-off approach.
materials.notes: Remelting needs a small fraction of the energy of primary smelting.

materials.name: Stainless steel
materials.basis: Illustrative; typical mixed-route stainless with moderate scrap content.
materials.notes: Alloying elements (chromium, nickel) drive much of the impact; very long service life.

materials.name: Mild steel
materials.basis: Illustrative; global average mix of blast-furnace and electric-arc routes.
materials.notes: Needs coating or paint for corrosion protection.

materials.name: Glass
materials.basis: Illustrative; container glass with typical cullet content.
materials.notes: Low impact per kg but heavy — products usually need far more mass than plastic equivalents.

materials.name: Cardboard
materials.basis: Illustrative; corrugated board with mixed virgin and recycled fibre. Biogenic carbon excluded.
materials.notes: Renewable and widely recycled; loses strength when wet.

materials.name: Paper
materials.basis: Illustrative; virgin-fibre paper. Biogenic carbon excluded.

alternatives.cost: Usually cost-neutral to slightly cheaper than virgin paper.
trade_offs: Slightly lower brightness and fibre strength.
Fibres can only be recycled a limited number of times, so some virgin input to the overall system is always needed.

materials.name: Recycled paper
materials.basis: Illustrative; recovered-fibre paper with the cut-off approach.
materials.notes: Lower water and energy demand than virgin pulping.

materials.name: Cotton (conventional)
materials.basis: Illustrative; fibre cultivation and ginning. Water use varies by an order of magnitude with irrigation practice and region.
materials.notes: Very water-intensive; fertiliser and pesticide use are significant.

alternatives.cost: Organic fibre typically carries a noticeable price premium.
alternatives.feasibility_note: Certified supply is limited and needs chain-of-custody documentation.
trade_offs: Lower yields per hectare can mean more land is needed for the same fibre.
Published water and carbon savings are contested and depend heavily on region and irrigation.
Dyeing and finishing impacts are unchanged.

materials.name: Organic cotton
materials.basis: Illustrative and deliberately conservative; the size of any saving over conventional cotton is debated in the literature.
materials.notes: No synthetic pesticides or fertilisers; typically lower yields.

materials.name: Bamboo
materials.basis: Illustrative; engineered/laminated bamboo. Biogenic carbon storage excluded.
materials.notes: Fast-growing; adhesives and long transport distances can offset benefits.

materials.name: Wood
materials.basis: Illustrative; kiln-dried sawn timber. Biogenic carbon storage excluded.
materials.notes: Low processing impact; depends on responsible forestry.
